extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 challenge samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were curated from six existing benchmarks (MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista). An automated filtering pipeline evaluated an initial pool of 22,401 samples using eight LLM inspectors (two closed-source and six open-source 20B+ LLMs under 2-shot setting) to identify and exclude questions answerable without images (hit count > 2). The remaining 11,607 candidate samples were categorized by difficulty using 16 LVLMs, followed by manual review and curation by three experts to finalize 1,500 samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were transformed/verified to be converted into a multiple-choice format to ensure consistent evaluation and enable heuristic matching rules for accuracy calculation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Initial candidate pool of 22,401 samples was filtered using eight LLMs to eliminate samples with hit counts greater than 2, narrowing it down to 11,607 candidate samples. Hit counts of 16 LVLMs were then tallied to split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three human experts conducted manual reviews to ensure: 1) each sample's answer is strictly based on understanding visual content; 2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes; 3) samples require advanced multi-modal abilities, resulting in 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated inspection pipeline utilizing GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, and Deepseek-67B.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLMs' and LVLMs' training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing multi-modal evaluations often suffer from lack of visual dependency and unintended training data leakage. For MMStar, the benchmark is currently limited to 1,500 samples, and the authors plan to expand it into an online dynamic evaluation benchmark in future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating the multi-modal perception, reasoning, and comprehension capabilities of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), as well as measuring multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML).
